summary: CCC-built 20-foot pole tower finished in 1937 on Thunderbolt Mountain near Deer Lodge; destroyed or removed 1965-66; its Jack Mountain replacement was torn down in 2011.

facts.design: 20-foot pole L-4 tower with a glass enclosure
facts.status_note: Gone since 1965-66; no source describes what, if anything, remains at the Thunderbolt site

staffing.status: manned in July 1938; no later staffing found

events.note: Built by the Thunderbolt CCC camp; work began July 1937 and was completed that fall
Manned by July 1938, in preparation for prevention control, along with Haystack lookout
Jack Mountain tower, a separate site, built in 1965 as the replacement
January 1966 item says the old station was removed when the new Jack Mountain tower replaced it
The Jack Mountain replacement was torn down in 2011; this is a different structure on a different peak

resolved_conflicts.explanation: firelookout.com gives 8,597 feet. Three 1937 newspaper items quoted by montanalookouts.weebly.com give 8,000, 8,400 and 9,400 feet. The story reports all four.

firelookout.com says destroyed in 1965. The January 1966 newspaper item says the old station was removed when the Jack Mountain tower replaced it. The Jack Mountain tower was built in 1965, so the two accounts fit together.

notes_for_editor: Built 1937 by the Thunderbolt CCC camp with 1938 staffing, but sources give no fire record and nothing on the site today. Elevation conflicts across sources (8,597 vs 8,000, 8,400 and 9,400 ft). Do not confuse with the Thunderbolt Mountain Lookout in Idaho (us/id, NHLR) or the Thunderbolt Mountain in Flathead/Lake County (Ground Gone); both are different towers. The Jack Mountain replacement (FFLOS US 1945, MT 8) is a separate site and is covered only as context.
